cues.text: Model Context Protocol, or MCP, is an open standard that allows AI models to securely connect to external tools, data sources, and services — making them far more capable and context-aware.
Here you can see the overall architecture of the Model Context Protocol system.
Let's explore how MCP actually works.

The host application — for example, Claude Desktop — acts as an MCP client. It discovers MCP servers, which are lightweight processes that expose Tools, Resources, and Prompts over a local or remote transport layer.
This diagram shows the client-server communication flow inside MCP.
Now let's look at building your first MCP server.

Use the SDK to register tools with registerTool(), expose file resources with registerResource(), and define reusable prompt templates with registerPrompt(). Deploy via stdio or HTTP over SSE transport.
The code sample here shows a minimal MCP server implementation.
